dialect.detail: Likely Micro Focus Visual COBOL or similar Windows-oriented dialect; program-id uses AS clause with dotted namespace string 'exam2012.Program1', suggesting .NET or Visual COBOL targeting. No EXEC CICS/SQL, uses indexed file I/O with ISAM-style organization.
evidence: open i-o / open input / open output pattern

purpose.domain_detail: Inpatient medical records management system (exmedecinpatient = 'exam medecin inpatient' in French). Manages doctors (medecins), patients, consultations, and interventions with cost tracking.
purpose.summary: A French-language interactive menu-driven program for managing medical inpatient records. It supports creating and deleting doctors and patients, creating consultations and interventions linked to doctors and patients, listing patients of a given doctor, and displaying total costs for a patient. All data is stored in indexed ISAM files.

notable_features: Multiple indexed files with alternate record keys and duplicates
program-id AS clause with dotted namespace (Micro Focus / .NET style)
Inline comments using '///////' style (non-standard, treated as code lines)
No COPY statements, no CALL statements
PERFORM UNTIL with inline READ AT END pattern
verdict.notes: The file is decoded with latin-1, consistent with French accented characters (é, è, etc.) in display strings. The '///////' comment-like lines are not standard COBOL comment syntax (which uses '*' in column 7 for fixed format); they appear as code lines and would likely cause compile errors or be treated as division markers depending on the compiler. The program-id AS clause strongly suggests Micro Focus Visual COBOL or .NET COBOL. The overall structure and naming ('exam2012') suggest a student exam exercise from 2012.
